title: Elderwyld as continent/world layer
summary: Elderwyld is the continent/world layer: a frontier land on the edge of reality shaped by divine aftermath, the Nameless Goddess's sacrifice, unstable borders with unreality, and old/pre-era structures under ordinary landscapes.
must_not_claim: Mirathorn is the continent
this was retrieved from C1S1-C1S3 session memory

title: Mirathorn as city destination node
summary: Mirathorn is a major Elderwyld city-state at the base of the Stormspire Peaks by Lake Mirathorn, with trade, brewing, fishing, agriculture, magical goods, Stormspire Academy, city gates, outtown, and the Festival of Expansion.
must_not_claim: Mirathorn final approach describes the entire Stone Bridge route
Mirathorn is Elderwyld itself

title: Final approach to Mirathorn from the east
summary: The approach to Mirathorn from the east includes lush farms, orchards, vineyards, livestock, floatgoats, mills, breweries, workshops, smithies, crowded festival traffic, outtown tents, tolls, guards, and potential Shepherd's Flock protest tension.
must_not_claim: the party reaches Mirathorn in C1S4
the whole Stone Bridge-to-Mirathorn road is known

title: Reaches as Elderwyld distance language
summary: A Reach is an Elderwyld distance unit equal to 8 kilometers or 5 miles, culturally tied to early settlement and the experience of extending safety into the unknown.
must_not_claim: exact Stone Bridge-to-Mirathorn distance is known from this card

title: Fantastic livestock of Elderwyld
summary: Elderwyld domestic ecology includes Luminox Sheep, Tidal Turtles, Starling Cows, Sunflower Ducks, Flutter Ferrets, and Float Goats. These animals make farms feel magical while still practical.
must_not_claim: all these animals appear on the Stone Bridge road unless selected by GM

title: General Elderwyld road grammar
summary: Elderwyld roads mix mundane logistics with weird pressure: mud, bridge repairs, tolls, convoys, pilgrims, refugees, storms, hamlets, predators, cult hints, bad maps, liminal events, and sudden hard turns.
must_not_claim: Mireward Reach is the Stone Bridge-to-Mirathorn road
encounter table results definitely occur

title: Mireward Reach is north from Mirathorn, not automatically C1S4 road
summary: The Mireward Reach is the road north from Mirathorn toward fen and swamp country. It is useful Elderwyld road grammar, but should not be treated as the Stone Bridge-to-Mirathorn route without a linking source.
must_not_claim: Stone Bridge lies on the Mireward Reach
Campaign 1 uses Campaign 2 route distances

title: Missing Stone Bridge-to-Mirathorn route gazetteer
summary: The repo search did not surface a clean route gazetteer for the Stone Bridge-to-Mirathorn leg. A good planner should admit this gap while using C1S3 for destination, Mirathorn world docs for endpoint approach, and Elderwyld ecology for labeled support flavor.
must_not_claim: exact route is known
exact intermediate villages are canon

title: Pre-era conical hills in Elderwyld plains
summary: Some Elderwyld plains contain odd grassy conical hills with still ponds on top. Player-facing, they are lonely hills; GM-facing, they are engineered pre-era structures such as ward anchors, vent systems, old works, or sealed doors.
must_not_claim: these hills are on the Stone Bridge route unless adapted
players know the hills are artificial

title: Night camp on a conical hill
summary: Camping on conical hills can produce watch prompts: odd smoke, pond reflections, humming stones, strange dreams, small animals, moving lights, weather pressure, and occasional geomantic drake activity.
must_not_claim: the party camps on such a hill unless GM chooses it

title: Geomantic drakes as pre-era signal creatures
summary: Geomantic drakes are draconic-adjacent creatures drawn to buried workings, conical high points, wells, ward anchors, and old geomantic charge. They molt, nest, ground energy, and cache shiny or story-rich objects like corvids.
must_not_claim: geomantic drakes are involved in Hempholm unless adapted
drake nests are on every road

title: Migrating Forest pressure logic
summary: The Migrating Forest is a reactive wilderness where the forest notices pressure, remembers actions, shifts routes, distorts navigation, tests resources, draws dinosaurs, carries storm residue, and may involve Branchbound guidance or judgment.
must_not_claim: the Stone Bridge-to-Mirathorn route passes through the Migrating Forest unless sourced

title: Campaign 2 Mireward tracker as non-backportable reference
summary: Campaign 2 travel notes give a northbound Mireward Reach tracker: Mossford about two days from Mirathorn, a Deep Reach milestone about five days from Mirathorn, open plains, low hills, and hilltop ponds. Use as bookkeeping pattern, not Campaign 1 route canon.
must_not_claim: Mossford is on the C1S4 route
Campaign 2 distances apply to Campaign 1

title: Safe travel generation guidance for C1S4 Q3
summary: For Q3, a planner should combine C1S3's Mirathorn destination vector with Mirathorn endpoint imagery and labeled Elderwyld road ecology, while explicitly warning that exact Stone Bridge-to-Mirathorn route details remain missing.
must_not_claim: generated road details are canon
world support equals session memory
